proof_audit.topic: Finite Bayes normalization, prediction and decision
proof_audit.assumptions: Proper finite prior, positive observation marginal, ordered Bernoulli likelihood; future records iid conditional on the shared parameter.
proof_audit.argument: Sequential conditioning multiplies observation probabilities into evidence. Summing the four future records gives the predictive count distribution. E[Y1Y2|data]=E[theta²|data], so covariance is posterior Var(theta), generally positive despite conditional independence. Launch utility 3p_high-2(1-p_high)=5p_high-2 gives indifference at 2/5.
proof_audit.scope: Proper-prior sensitivity is real decision sensitivity. Posterior probabilities do not establish frequentist coverage or robustness to an incorrect likelihood.
proof_audit.judgment: Valid finite proof and correctly separated uncertainty interpretations.

proof_audit.topic: MH balance, minorization and Monte Carlo precision
proof_audit.assumptions: Finite positive target, stochastic proposal with reverse support; the convergence result additionally has the displayed positive minorization. Stationary variance and a low initial state at time 0 are separate sampling laws.
proof_audit.argument: Accepted off-diagonal target flow is min(pi_i q_ij,pi_j q_ji). Symmetry yields balance, and row complements yield stochasticity; summing gives invariance. For P=delta Pi+(1-delta)R, stochastic R contracts total variation of signed zero-mass differences, proving convergence and unique stationarity when delta>0. Delta=1 means independent target rows. The high indicator is lumpable because both non-high rows have equal high-transition probability. Its centered eigenfunction has lambda=50/81; stationary covariance gamma_k=gamma_0 lambda^k follows by conditional expectation. Counting lag pairs yields exact finite variance; geometric summability gives an O(1/n) bound and L2 convergence. The long variance multiplier is (1+lambda)/(1-lambda).
proof_audit.initialized_and_changed_laws: From low time 0, E[f(X_t)]=pi_high(1-lambda^t), sampled at t=1,...,4. Its finite variance differs from stationary variance. q=pi produces independent draws after the first transition. Laziness gives (1+lambda)/2 and increases positive-correlation inflation here. Zero reverse proposal support rejects a one-way move.
proof_audit.scope: Balance alone is not convergence. The finite covariance/variance argument is not an unstated general MCMC CLT or a consistent practical variance estimator.
proof_audit.judgment: Complete scoped finite proof with correct target, initialization and covariance distinctions.

proof_audit.topic: Lasso optimization, sparse constants and duplicate coefficients
proof_audit.assumptions: Loss ||y-Xb||²/(2n), lambda>0, every coefficient including the constant penalized. Exact support size s>=1, noise-score infinity norm<=lambda/2, full-vector unsquared cone condition ||Xv||/sqrt(n)>=kappa||v||2.
proof_audit.argument: Positive lambda makes the objective coercive; continuity gives attainment on a compact sublevel. Derivatives off zero and both one-sided derivatives at zero give KKT necessity. Convexity plus an l1 subgradient proves sufficiency. Orthonormal Gram completion of squares gives soft thresholding. Strict convexity in fits and convexity of the penalty give unique fitted values without unique coefficients. Comparing the optimum to beta* gives prediction/(2n)+(lambda/2)||Delta_Sc||1<=(3lambda/2)||Delta_S||1, hence cone ratio 3. With t=||XDelta||/sqrt(n), t²<=3lambda sqrt(s)||Delta||2 and t>=kappa||Delta||2 imply l2<=3lambda sqrt(s)/kappa², prediction/n<=9lambda²s/kappa² and l1<=12lambda s/kappa²; Delta=0 is immediate.
proof_audit.gaussian_event: Fixed columns with norms<=sqrt(n) and Gaussian errors give score variance<=sigma²/n. Two Chernoff tails and a p-column union bound yield 2p exp(-nt²/(2sigma²)); set t=lambda/2. Column-score independence is unnecessary. This proves neither curvature nor support recovery.
proof_audit.duplicate_proof: For t=b1+b2, |b1|+|b2|>=|t| reduces the scalar objective to (2-t)²/2+|t|/2 with unique t=3/2. Equality requires the entire nonnegative split segment. Opposite coefficients give a nonzero null direction inside the support-{1} cone, so positive full-vector curvature fails. Weighted penalty (1,2) obeys |b1|+2|b2|>=|t|+|b2|, forcing (3/2,0) at the same lower bound. This is penalty selection without new identifying data.
proof_audit.judgment: Constants, norm, all-coefficient penalty, whole minimizer set and scope of statistical claims are correct.

proof_audit.assumptions: Consistency, no interference, exchangeability given X, true overlap, integrable potential outcomes. Expected-score identities require absolute integrability of their terms. Uniformly clipped candidate e and integrable candidate regressions suffice. Orthogonality uses bounded perturbations and a common c>0 for true and path propensities.
proof_audit.argument: Conditional score expectation replaces residual numerators by e0(m1-g1) and (1-e0)(m0-g0). Subtracting m1-m0 yields (e-e0)[(g1-m1)/e+(g0-m0)/(1-e)]. Under qualified integrability the tower step gives the population remainder. Clipping and Cauchy-Schwarz give the c^-1 L2 product bound. On e=e0+t a and gd=md+t bd, remainder is t² E[a(b1/e+b0/(1-e))]. Common c and bounded perturbations bound the expectation uniformly; division by t gives zero derivative.
proof_audit.variance_and_cancellation: At truth, conditional-effect variance 1/4 plus conditional residual variance 16/3 yields V=67/12. Cross terms vanish by zero conditional residual means and disjoint treatment indicators. At e=1/2, regression errors +1,-1 cancel the bracket pointwise, but their score variance changes. Double robustness gives sufficient rather than necessary zero-bias conditions.
proof_audit.judgment: Valid after canonical refinement. The independent integrability counterexample below explains why the qualification is substantive.

proof_audit.assumptions: Iid data; fixed K and predetermined/independent partition with positive limiting proportions; each fit, tuning and preprocessing uses only the outside sample. Bounded outcome/regressions, true and fitted overlap c, a,b=o_p(1), sqrt(N)ab=o_p(1), positive oracle variance.
proof_audit.argument: Condition on one outside training sample and the partition at a time. Its held-out records remain iid independent of its fit. Exact remainder gives |Pr|<=ab/c; score expansion gives ||r||2<=b/c+2Ba/c². Conditional variance of the held-out mean is at most Pr²/n_k. Conditional Chebyshev at root-N scale bounds error probability by min(1,(N/n_k)Pr²/epsilon²). This converges in probability to zero and is bounded by one; splitting at a fixed threshold gives convergence of its expectation. Repeat separately for finitely many folds, without asserting joint independence of fitted functions. The remainder sum is negligible and the original iid oracle CLT applies.
proof_audit.variance: Conditional Markov, truncated at one, makes pooled empirical r² vanish. Uniform bounded scores and Cauchy-Schwarz transfer second moments. Oracle LLN and mean consistency give Vhat->V, then Slutsky gives standard error sqrt(Vhat/N).
proof_audit.scope: The finite eight-row example does not prove coverage. Cross-fitting alone supplies neither causal identification nor learner consistency/product rates. No general unbounded-score, dependent-data, growing-fold or efficiency theorem is claimed.
proof_audit.judgment: Complete conditioning, conditional-to-unconditional and variance-consistency arguments.

proof_audit.topic: Finite-cell rates, quarter-rate bias and leakage
proof_audit.assumptions: Case-4 bounded iid law with positive cell probabilities>=1/8; training sizes proportional to N. The rate counterexample uses true nuisances plus deterministic perturbations. The identifier is an independent continuous random variable.
proof_audit.argument: Bounded numerator/denominator cell averages have root-n error. On Bn>=b/2, (An-mBn)/Bn has root-n error; the complement tends to zero. Empty cells occur with probability (1-b)^n. Laplace smoothing adds O(1/n); clipping is nonexpansive relative to truths in the intervals. Finite cells/folds give L2 O_p(N^-1/2). Exponents 1/5+1/3 give root-N product N^-1/30; two big-O quarter rates yield only O_p(1). For t=N^-1/4, e=e0+t/8, g1=m1+t, g0=m0, exact bias=t²[1/(2+t)+1/(6+t)]/2 and scaled limit=1/3.
proof_audit.leakage: Conditional on a finite training sample, a fresh continuous identifier hits none of its IDs almost surely. Overwriting both regressions with each own-row Y only on that set leaves fresh-population L2 errors zero. Reused scores nevertheless vanish pointwise. Proper held-out identifiers avoid this exceptional set, recovering the oracle score but not supplying all other assumptions.
proof_audit.judgment: Actual trained learner, theoretical rate sequence and invalid own-sample reuse are properly distinguished.

proof_audit.topic: BH leave-one-out and independent super-uniform nulls
proof_audit.assumptions: Finite fixed family, q in (0,1), inclusive thresholds, and each true-null p independent of the entire other-p vector and super-uniform. False-null p-values may depend mutually.
proof_audit.argument: At the largest passing index R exactly R values lie below qR/m, else a larger index would pass. Replacing p_i by zero gives R_i>=1 and R_i>=R. If i was rejected, ordered values above R are unchanged and R_i=R. Conversely, restoring p_i<=qR_i/m leaves at least R_i passing values, forcing R>=R_i; thus equality and rejection. Therefore its FDP contribution is 1{p_i<=qR_i/m}/R_i. Conditional on all other p-values, super-uniformity plus independence bounds expectation by q/m. Summing gives FDR<=m0 q/m.
proof_audit.laws_and_scope: The discrete uniform grid CDF floor(12u)/12 is super-uniform and attains equality at relevant thresholds, yielding exact FDR 1/6. The four-point dependent complete-null law has valid marginal jumps but BH rejection probability 3/20 at q=1/10. Complete-null FDR=FWER while every nonempty list has FDP=1. In the independent mixed-null example E[V]/E[R]=3/11 differs from E[FDP]=1/6.
proof_audit.judgment: Both directions, ties, zero rejections and expectation/realized-list limits are correct. Marginal validity alone is expressly insufficient.

prompt_solution_audit.independent_solution: Audit six distinct claims: conditional posterior belief versus sampling coverage; correctly targeted correlated MCMC versus iid evidence; KKT optimum versus true support/identification; predictive performance versus causal assumptions; held-out scoring versus learner consistency/product rate and variance; and expected FDP under a specified joint law versus a guarantee for every list. Concrete evidence includes the changed prior, wrong chain target/covariance, duplicate minimizers, stated exchangeability/overlap target, quarter-rate or ID leakage, and independent/dependent BH laws. Six domains total 12 points, one distinction point and one evidence/qualified-replacement point each. Alternative correct arguments are accepted; generic warnings alone earn at most one per domain.
prompt_solution_audit.answer_comparison: All six false claims have specific benchmark corrections and transparent argument-based scoring.
prompt_solution_audit.exact_prompt: A report claims: “Our posterior is a confidence guarantee; a million MCMC steps are iid evidence; lasso selected the true variables because its solver converged; predictive accuracy establishes causality; cross-fitting automatically gives root-N inference; and BH ensures at most q of every discovery list is false.” Write a research audit using the chapter's evidence. Score the response out of 12 using the six-domain rubric below; each domain must state the correct distinction and a concrete check, counterexample or qualified replacement claim.

instruction_and_assessment.coverage: Canonical objective and all six coverage strands taught; every new finite-chain, regularization, cross-fit and testing lemma required by exercises is derived locally.
instruction_and_assessment.prerequisites: Six flat links to established Bayes, testing, limit, linear algebra, causal and structural chapters. Runtime validates permitted syntax rather than requiring extra files in isolation.
instruction_and_assessment.definitions: Targets, prior/likelihood, initialization, full-vector curvature, training information, true/fitted nuisances, stochastic rates, FDR/FWER and empty rejection are defined before principal use.
instruction_and_assessment.rubric: Six domains at two points each total twelve. Each awards one distinction point and one concrete evidence or qualified replacement point. Generic correct warnings capped at one; false claims zero; alternative valid arguments allowed.
instruction_and_assessment.teach_back: Answered benchmark uses wrong MH target, duplicate design and quarter-rate counterexamples to separate computation, identifying variation, training reuse, causal assumptions and rates.
instruction_and_assessment.retention: Answered delayed prompt gives basic inequality constants, omitted stationary covariance sum, AIPW product remainder and largest inclusive BH passing index.

findings.issue: Pointwise positivity alone does not justify a uniformly bounded expectation along the orthogonality path; initial population identities also need integrability.
findings.resolution: Canonical additions require integrable potential outcomes, absolute integrability of expected-score terms with sufficient clipped candidate/integrable-regression conditions, and a common c for bounded perturbation paths.
findings.peer_assessment: Every exact replacement read and reconstructed. These conditions justify tower expectations and bounded path remainders without changing finite answers.

findings.origin: Independent peer analytic counterexample communicated before final binding
findings.severity: Independent support for the integrability refinement
findings.issue: Correct regressions with an arbitrary merely pointwise-positive candidate e need not yield a defined unconditional AIPW mean.
findings.construction: Let X~Uniform(0,1), D independent Bernoulli(1/2), and both potential outcomes independent fair signs, independent of X,D. Then m0=m1=0, e0=1/2, with bounded outcomes and the causal assumptions. Choose g0=g1=0 but e(X)=X. Score is D epsilon1/X-(1-D)epsilon0/(1-X). Conditional mean is zero for each X, yet E|psi|=(1/2) integral_0^1 [1/x+1/(1-x)] dx=infinity. Symmetry makes both positive and negative parts have infinite expectation, so E psi is undefined.
findings.resolution: Final expected-score identities require absolute integrability; the explicit uniformly clipped sufficient condition excludes this case.
findings.status: resolved by the same canonical promotion

computation_and_domains.arithmetic: Exact fractions for laws, accepted flows, stationary systems, occupation counts, active KKT faces, conditional moments, fits and testing. Floating log/exp/sqrt only for Gaussian tuning and its tail check. Parsed exact fractions compare exactly.
computation_and_domains.budget: At most 12 probability states/linear-system dimension, 16 ordered observations, binary occupancy horizon 32, lasso four columns/16 rows, two-fold data 32 rows, testing family 12. Actual lasso fits use 27 faces; original testing law has 144 states. No random grid or unbounded simulation.
computation_and_domains.failures: Boolean/nonfinite/oversized scalars; signed/unnormalized probabilities; zero evidence; Bernoulli domain/budget; target/proposal shape; occupancy budget; zero penalty/singular oracle design/response shape; treatment/overlap; fold/covariate/outcome bounds; family/p-value/q/rule; duplicate-key/nonfinite/overflow JSON; unsafe visible expression.
computation_and_domains.domain_scope: The full-rank active-face oracle is deliberately distinct from the analytic duplicate-column proof. Its singular-design rejection does not assert that lasso lacks a minimizer.
computation_and_domains.proof_scope: Finite checks support concrete results and boundaries. Asymptotic, integrability, cone, leakage and FDR proofs were reviewed analytically, not established by finite numerical testing.
